To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new thiol-specific labeling reagent, 5-iodoacetamide-2,4-dinitrophenyl fluorescein (IA-DNP), has been synthesized and characterized, and that this reagent has been successfully applied in labeling of proteins, including hemoglobin and myoglobin.
a novel fluorophore, BMTA, has been designed and synthesized, and that BMTA is a small and highly specific reagent for labeling of proteins and peptides at cysteines.

a new thiol-specific probe introduces a small bis (methylamino) terephthalic acid fluorochrome into proteins and the noninvasive probe, with distinct spectroscopic characteristics, is a powerful tool in the studies of protein folding, protein redox reactions, and other protein functions.

developing new chemical probes for studying protein folding and hemes redox reactions.

developing new chemical tools to probe the structure, function and dynamics of biological systems, with an emphasis on protein folding, protein redox reactions and metalloprotein structure and function.
the synthesis of novel fluorescent probes for biological studies.
